{"record_id":"fun2026_zombie_high_dimensional_grid","stage":"BASELINE_AUDIT","arm":"neutral","iteration":0,"parent_sha256":"3253ebd62bc77fc66beea8a88fa1afd3e97a36244c8e7d06450bea0403614e36","complete":true,"claims":[{"idx":0,"claim":"For every fixed k≥1, th_z((P_n)^{□k})=Ω_k(n^{k/(k+1)}).","claim_sha256":"f69b11c85f67d128dab73558ee41a1d5c7d958fd9c26f29ac07da1e209661cff","verdict":"VERIFIED","evidence":"If p zombies capture within t rounds, every grid vertex must be within initial L1-distance t of a zombie; otherwise a survivor starting there and remaining stationary cannot be reached in t moves. Each such ball is contained in an L∞ cube of at most (2t+1)^k vertices, so n^k≤p(2t+1)^k. With x=p+t, p≤x and, since p≥1, 2t+1≤3x. Hence n^k≤3^k x^(k+1), yielding x≥3^(-k/(k+1))n^(k/(k+1)). This holds for every admissible p and therefore after throttling minimization.","witness":"none","search_method":"Direct deductive audit of the covering argument, game quantifiers, and exponent algebra using only the authorized source and draft.","checker_path":"none"},{"idx":1,"claim":"Mesh capture lemma: for each r≥1 there are constants M_r,A_r such that, on every r-dimensional Cartesian grid with coordinate meshes containing both endpoints and having gaps at most d, placing M_r zombies at every mesh intersection guarantees capture in at most A_r d rounds.","claim_sha256":"2e9e0bbfbbc45bddb3dc119c12fb6dec4d4eef40e6840ec7384dc76ac3da14f7","verdict":"VERIFIED","evidence":"The stated induction is sound with M_1=A_1=1, M_r=2rM_{r-1}, and A_r=(r+1)(A_{r-1}+1). In dimension one, a survivor either starts on an occupied mesh point or is bracketed by consecutive mesh zombies whose separation contracts until capture. For the induction, put R=A_{r-1}d. On each side in coordinate i, either the boundary is within R or the mesh-gap condition supplies a mesh hyperplane at distance in [R,R+d). Each of the 2r labeled hyperplanes receives a disjoint projected (r−1)-dimensional team; 2rM_{r-1} copies at an intersection suffice even when labels meet there. A projected move changes a mismatching non-i coordinate toward the survivor, so it is also a legal full-grid shortest-path move. Each team produces an i-guard within R rounds. A nonboundary plane cannot be strictly crossed in R moves; reaching it on the last move either meets an already aligned guard or uses coordinate i and therefore cannot simultaneously create a new projected alignment. Boundaries cannot be crossed. Once obtained, a guard repairs the unique projected mismatch caused by the preceding survivor move, or advances in coordinate i when already aligned. Thus it remains on its assigned side. After synchronization, let W be the sum of the r lower-to-upper guard separations. Initially W<2r(R+d). Following a survivor move in coordinate j, the two j-guards advance and reduce W by 2 while all other guards repair coordinate j; after a stay, every pair advances. Hence every noncapture round reduces W by at least 2. Capture follows within r(R+d)=r(A_{r-1}+1)d further rounds, and R+1+r(A_{r-1}+1)d≤A_rd for integer d≥1. Degenerate one-vertex grids are captured initially.","witness":"none","search_method":"Reconstructed the induction from first principles and audited team allocation, shortest-path legality, boundary timing, guard invariants, potential decrease, and degenerate cases.","checker_path":"none"},{"idx":2,"claim":"Consequently, for every fixed k≥3, th_z((P_n)^{□k})=Θ_k(n^{k/(k+1)})=Θ_k(|G|^{1/(k+1)}); in particular the k=3 endpoint is complete.","claim_sha256":"5dae3b72eeda2c6203a2e6720cb139ef44a8270f50022b2f0f89fccca542ec6d","verdict":"VERIFIED","evidence":"Using the endpoint-augmented mesh {0,d,2d,…,n−1} gives gaps at most d and at most n/d+2 mesh coordinates per dimension. Claim 1 therefore supplies p≤M_k(n/d+2)^k zombies and capture time at most A_kd. For d=ceil(n^(k/(k+1))), both p and A_kd are O_k(n^(k/(k+1))). For sufficiently large n this placement uses at most n^k zombies; finitely many smaller n are covered by occupying every vertex. Claim 0 supplies the matching lower bound. Since |G|=n^k, n^(k/(k+1))=|G|^(1/(k+1)). The recurrences give M_2=4, A_2=6, M_3=24, and A_3=28, so k=3 is included rather than merely approached conditionally.","witness":"none","search_method":"Direct asymptotic substitution and symbolic verification of mesh cardinality, recurrence constants, small-n handling, and the conversion from n to |G|.","checker_path":"none"}],"confirmed_refutations":[],"target_verdict":"FULLY_RESOLVES_TARGET","claimed_resolution_verdict":"ACCURATE","target_evidence":"The exact target asks for the fixed-dimensional Cartesian grid result for every fixed k≥3, with a complete k=3 endpoint. The verified lower bound and mesh upper bound prove precisely th_z((P_n)^{□k})=Theta_k(|G|^(1/(k+1))) for every such k, and the argument explicitly includes k=3. This is neither a coarser bound nor a model/product mismatch. The draft's claimed_resolution of FULL and its affirmative final headline are therefore accurate.","overall":"VERIFIED","checks_performed":["Read only the two authorized JSON files and did not use the web, retrieval material, prior runs, or reports.","Checked the stationary-survivor covering necessity and lower-bound algebra.","Reconstructed the full mesh induction, including simultaneous projected teams, duplicate-team capacity at intersecting hyperplanes, shortest-path legality, crossing timing, guard maintenance, and the separation potential.","Checked the recurrence inequality and the k=3 constants M_3=24 and A_3=28 symbolically.","Checked the mesh-size asymptotics, admissible-zombie-count issue for large n, finite small-n fallback, and |G| exponent conversion.","No finite counterexample or computational claim required a persisted checker; all verdicts are deductive."]}--- END INDEPENDENT AUDIT ---
